The first use of ostracism in Athens, in 487 BCE, when the citizens voted to send Hipparchus son of Charmus, a relative of the old tyrant family, into exile for ten years.

Ostracism was part of the reforms credited to Cleisthenes. Once a year the assembly decided whether to hold one. If so, each citizen scratched a name on a broken pot, an ostrakon. If enough votes were cast, the man named most often had to leave Athens for ten years, but he kept his property and citizenship. It was a way to remove someone too powerful before he could become a tyrant.

In the 480s it struck the friends of the tyrants, then leading politicians:

  • Aristides in 482 BCE
  • Themistocles around 471 BCE
  • Cimon in 461 BCE

Thousands of ostraca have been dug up in Athens. The last ostracism was around 416 BCE. It is a distinctive tool of Athenian democracy.
sum: The first use of ostracism in Athens, in 487 BCE, when the citizens voted to send Hipparchus son of Charmus, a relative of the old tyrant family, into exile for ten years.
